title: The Sky-Blue Pebble
story:
James sat by the edge of the Whispering Brook, his toes still tingling from the cool water. He remembered the wild, dense green of his familiar jungle home. He remembered the vast, sun-dappled expanse of the meadow he had just crossed. Now, he listened to the water. The water did not rush; it murmured. The water did not push; it invited.

Whenever James felt the vastness of the world pressing in on him, he counted. He counted the white wildflowers dancing on the bank—one, two, three. He counted the ripples curving around a mossy log—one, two, three, four. He counted the tiny, silvery fish darting beneath the surface—one, two, three, four, five. This was his ritual, his quiet way of telling the world that he was listening, and that he was keeping track of its secrets.

Reaching into the shallow pool, his fingers brushed against something remarkably smooth. He pulled it out: a perfectly round, sky-blue pebble. It was wonderfully cold, holding the chill of the high mountains far beyond the meadow. He turned it over in his palm, marveling at its texture. He had never held a stone so blue. He had never felt a stone so cold. He had never known a stone could feel so much like a fallen piece of the sky.

James slipped the blue pebble carefully into his pocket for safekeeping, pleased with his new treasure. He looked down the length of the brook, watching how the water traveled onward, disappearing into a shadow of weeping willows in the distance. A single yellow leaf floated past, riding the gentle current like a tiny boat bound for an unknown sea. He wondered where the water went when it was finally tired of running.
